challenges.name: mcp-session-quiz
challenges.title: Read an MCP session
challenges.description: Two excerpts from the codedev-enrollments server's traffic: what an initialize answer allows the client to call next, and how a failed tool call reaches the model.

questions.explanation: True. Capability negotiation is the contract of the session: the server listed tools and resources in its capabilities and left out prompts, so it has said it offers no prompts. Sending prompts/list anyway relies on behaviour the server never promised; at best it answers with a JSON-RPC error such as -32601 (method not found). The client should check result.capabilities before using a feature and simply not show a prompt menu for this server. The misconception is that every MCP server implements every method and capabilities are informational only.

questions.question:
The model called lookup_enrollment with a wrong course id. The server answered:

<- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Course not found: postgres-perf. Use the course public id, for example postgres-performance."}],"isError":true}}

A reviewer comments on the pull request: "This is a bug. A failure must be a JSON-RPC error object, otherwise the model never learns that the call failed."

Statement: "Because the server answered with a result and not a JSON-RPC error, the model is not told that the call failed."
questions.explanation: False. MCP reports tool execution failures inside a normal result with isError: true, precisely so that the host passes the message to the model as the tool's output. The model reads "Course not found ... use postgres-performance" and can retry with a correct id. A JSON-RPC error object is for protocol problems, such as an unknown tool name or a request that is not valid, and hosts usually treat it as a failure of the connection or request rather than as something for the model to fix. The misconception is that only an error object counts as a failure; here it would actually hide the useful message from the model.
